items.title: 52193_Jay McShann oral history interview
items.q: the only thing that I knew was that thing that I had heart Bessie Smith do, you know, which was backwater blues

ctx.x: Not everyday, no. Maybe this was just once every two weeks or something like that and like they would have a little pep meeting or something, they would call it. The principal might talk about something or somebody else talk about something and then they might have somebody to sing something. But he wanted me to play. And I says, "I can't play. I don't play. I can't play up there." So he says, "Just do what you did," and I didn't want to and I begged out of it. But I'll tell you what happened.

He called on me anyhow. So he called on me anyhow. So I went on up and the only thing that I knew was that thing that I had heart Bessie Smith do, you know, which was backwater blues, you know? And I just started playing that and the kids in school screamed and you know how they do and clapped their hands and screamed. And the next day in school, I caught it from everybody. items.title: Jay McShann interviewed by Monk Rowe, Sarasota, Florida, April 12, 1996
items.q: I think it was either Mamie or Bessie Smith, I don’t know which it one it was.

ctx.x: You’ve done so much in your career I barely know where to start, but what kind of music were you hearing as a child that led you to what you do?

Well I’ll tell you what I think really what brought that on. My dad used to work in a furniture store. Back in those days, remember those old Okeh records where they had the dog advertising, and they had the horn coming out of the record machine you know. And they used to sell those at the store where my dad worked. And so sometimes he’d bring a record player that wasn’t no good you know and he’d bring it home. And there was always two or three records laying around there in the truck or something. So one day I…
That was considered to be music that did not belong in the house. © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -2-
